Chapter 7

Smart Supplier Selection

  • Hatice Kübra Özensel
    Necmettin Erbakan University, Turkey
  • Burak Efe
    Necmettin Erbakan University, Turkey

ABSTRACT

Supplier selection, which is one of the phases of supply chain management, was examined in this chapter. In the line of four expert opinions and literature review, four main criteria, including environmental, economic, social, and smart criteria, and 18 sub-criteria were evaluated in this study. An interval-valued q-rung orthopair fuzzy (IVqROF) number based MAIRCA (multi attributive ideal-real comparative analysis) method is proposed for the ranking of 5 alternative suppliers. In this chapter, fuzzy number was proposed for the MAIRCA method, but unlike the literature, IVqROF number was applied to the MAIRCA method. It has been seen that the IVqROF number, which is the extension of the q-rung orthopair fuzzy number obtained by developing the intuitionistic fuzzy number and the Pythagorean fuzzy number, provides an advantage in evaluating expert opinions. In addition, Industry 4.0 criteria were examined under the smart criterion and contributed to the supplier selection problem. The study examined the smart supplier selection problem of an automotive sub-industry company.

INTRODUCTION

The retail market is growing day by day by becoming global, and the product produced in one continent can be used as raw material in another continent and sold to other continents. In addition to the advantages that this globalization brings, it also makes supply chain management more complex and difficult for companies. It pushes businesses to seek more systematic, technological and faster ways for sustainable supply chain management. Businesses that can build these systematic, sustainable supply chains and realize their competitiveness with error-free supply processes as well as the right product, provide a competitive advantage over other businesses in the same sector. Despite the importance of the supply chain, it is also seen that until a certain time, not many empirical studies have been carried out by experts on the definition and integration of supply chain management within all other business policies. Supplier selection is the first and one of the most significant links in the supply chain to reduce costs. Many businesses aim to establish strong ties and cooperate with their suppliers in order to rise their competitiveness, to comply with the planned delivery dates given to their customers with the least deviation, and to increase the effectiveness of management (Shin et al., 2000).

Supplier selection has become one of the most important management issues. Supplier selection aims to identify the supplier with the highest performance to consistently meet the needs of the business. Choosing the best supplier among many possible suppliers with various qualifications is a complex task (Guarnieri and Trojan, 2019).

Since customer and supplier relationships are very important in businesses, choosing the right suppliers requires much more than cost comparison and the choices are predicted by various quantitative and qualitative factors. Once a supplier is fully integrated into an adequately run and organized supply chain, that relationship has a long-term impact on the competitiveness. Therefore, the supplier selection problem has a very important role in organizing an effective system for the supply chain. The supplier selection problem aims to decrease purchasing risk, maximize value for the customer, and establish short and long term connections between the consumer and suppliers. Developments in smart technologies over the years inevitably affect supply chains. Advanced smart technologies positioned as components of Industry 4.0, such as the internet of things, cyber systems, big data and artificial intelligence, ensure that all links forming the supply chain are more perceptible, interpretable, predictable, controllable and optimized. Supply chains where these smart technologies are integrated are defined as smart supply chains.

Supply chains are subject to increasingly faced with natural, human-induced or technological risks such as natural disasters, transportation accidents, worker strikes, terrorist attacks due to globalization. The consequences of these factors cause supply chain disruptions due to losses in productivity, profit, competition and revenue. Therefore, making supply chains smart and sustainable has become a necessity to protect the customer from shortages and interruptions. A business with a sustainable supply chain perspective needs to both communicate with the supplier and satisfy the customer, government and shareholders. In addition, in order to produce sustainable products in a sustainable supply chain, sustainability criteria must be taken into consideration when selecting suitable suppliers (Hosseini and Khaled, 2019).

In smart supply chain management, smart technologies are used at every stage, from transportation to the analysis of operators' working processes, to provide higher sustainability in social, environmental and economic terms. Sustainable supplier selection is one of the most significant components for the continuity of this sustainability. Because the actions of suppliers have great importance for sub-companies to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. It is very important to use smart technologies in evaluation process to achieve this sustainability in selection of suppliers (Chen et al., 2020; Ghadimi et al., 2019).

Traditional supplier selection is largely based on criteria such as affordable price and close distance. With the use of smart information technologies in supply chains, that smart supplier selection criteria such as supplier information management, warehouse automation, digitalization in the logistics system and data security, have emerged (Hasan et al., 2020; Torğul and Paksoy, 2023).

In general, decision makers face many uncertain factors when providing decision preferences for on-demand suppliers. Supplier selection depends on cost, quality, performance, technology, etc. It is a complex problem involving many criteria. Therefore, in order to obtain a systematic supplier selection process in line with existing criteria, a method is needed in which the criteria can be evaluated and prioritized (Tam and Tummala, 2001).

RELATED WORKS

This chapter uses many abbreviations and it can be seen in Appendix 1. In the dealer selection study for a telecommunication company conducted by Tam et al., a review of the decision-making methods in the literature is presented in order to support the dealer selection process. Based on extensive research in the literature, the study proposes a model based on AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process) to include decision makers with conflicting goals. The result of the case study shows that AHP ensures decreasing the time for supplier selection (Tam and Tummala, 2001). An approach for supplier classification is proposed by integrating ELECTRE (Elemination and Choice Translating Reality English) TRI, which is used in classification problems, and hesitant fuzzy set. The proposed method is examined in the automotive industry (Galo et al., 2018). Kaya and Yet proposed DEMATEL (Decision Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory) method to form a knowledge-based Bayesian network in line with the information obtained from multiple experts. The proposed method is applied in a case study of supplier selection at an automobile manufacturer (Kaya and Yet, 2019). Liu et al. examined a hybrid multi criteria decision making (MCDM) model combining fuzzy-based BWM (Best Worst Method), VIKOR (Multi-Criteria Optimization and Compromise Solution), PT (Prospect Theory) methods to make innovative supplier selection in the electric vehicle industry (Liu et al. 2021). Bai et al. examined socially sustainable supplier selection using the fuzzy grey number, BWM (Best Worst Method) and TODIM integration (Bai et al., 2019). Liang et al. proposed the prospect theory-based distributed linguistic ORESTE (Organization Rangement et Syntese de Donnees Relationnelles) method to describe the three superiority relationships (preference, indifference, and incomparability) in terms of the limited rationality of the decision maker in line with flexible and intelligent criteria. It is applied in the selection of battery suppliers in new energy vehicles enterprises (Liang et al., 2022). Ghadimi et al. added Industry 4.0 criteria to the sustainable supplier selection problem (Ghadimi et al., 2019). Chen et al. propose the interval valued type-2 fuzzy set based TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution) and DEMATEL methods for smart supplier selection (Chen et al., 2020). Hasan et al. proposed fuzzy set based TOPSIS method to rank the alternative suppliers under logistics 4.0 (Hasan et al., 2020). Pınar and Boran proposed q rung orthopair fuzzy (q-ROF) number based TOPSIS and ELECTRE methods for supplier selection (Pınar and Boran, 2020). Alavi et al. determined the weights of economic, social and cyclical criteria for sustainable supplier selection by using fuzzy best-worst method (BWM). The supplier with the highest performance is defined by using fuzzy inference system (Alavi et al., 2021). Abdollahzadeh et al. (2023) handled fuzzy best- worst method and fuzzy gray relational analysis methods to select the food suppliers in hospitals. Bisht and Pal (2024) handle social network analysis considering the trust relationships among experts and suggest q rung orthopair fuzzy decision making framework for green supplier selection. Singh et al. (2024) used TODIM (TOmada de Decisao Interativa Multicriterio) method based fuzzy prospect theory for optimal hydrogen fuel cell component supplier selection. Meng et al. (2024) presented TOPSIS approach based on graph neural networks in Pythagorean fuzzy environment.

Although fuzzy sets are very successful in evaluating uncertainties, they are insufficient in explaining the degree of non-membership/hesitancy of decision makers. In order to fill this deficiency of fuzzy sets, Atanassov presented an intuitionistic fuzzy set model in which both membership and non-membership degrees can be evaluated (Atanassov, 1986; Ali et al., 2022).

Pythagorean fuzzy sets, which are considered an extension of intuitionistic fuzzy set models, were introduced as a result of the need for a wider definition range. In an intuitionistic fuzzy set, the sum of the membership and non-membership degrees is allowed to be at most 1, and if it is less than 1, the difference is defined as hesitancy. In Pythagorean fuzzy sets, the sum of the squares of the membership and non-membership degrees is allowed to be at most 1 for a wider definition range. However, Pythagorean fuzzy sets are also lacking in some real applications. In order to achieve more accurate results in these real practices, a generalized q-ROF sets model can adjust the restriction on membership and non-membership degrees from a parameter type as an extension of Pythagorean fuzzy sets (Ali et al., 2022).

Some studies used q rung orthopair fuzzy number for different areas such as natural gas pipeline project risk assessment (Efe and Efe, 2023b) and glove design (Efe and Efe, 2022). MAIRCA based on q rung orthopair fuzzy number was presented for selecting emergency service of patients. (Efe and Efe, 2023a). It seems that the q-ROF sets model and its hybrid structures, which are a powerful idea, attracted the attention of researchers and caused them to deepen their studies on it. One of these studies presented a hybrid structure integrating interval-valued fuzzy set and q-ROF set (Joshi et al., 2018).

This chapter contributes to the literature as follows:

  • •MAIRCA is extended by using interval valued q-ROF number unlike existing studies in the literature. This study simultaneously ensures the advantages of MAIRCA and interval valued q-ROF number. It ensures to prevent information loss of the experts for the weights of criteria and criteria based alternative evaluation.
  • •Smart supplier selection is a new trend. This chapter also handled Industry 4.0 criteria except traditional supplier selection criteria. It used a novel method, which is interval valued q-ROF number based MAIRCA, for smart supplier selection problem.

SOLUTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

In this part of the study, the application of this new proposed model in a company in the automotive sub-industry sector is shown. The specified business was established in 1988 and is one of the pioneers in its sector. In addition to Automotive, it also has over 1000 types of products in the Marine-Locomotive and Stationary Engine groups. Table 1 shows the pseudo code of the proposed method.

Table 1. The pseudo code

Inputs: The expert group, criteria, alternatives, the judgments of expert group, the value of q
-begin
-Start algorithm and data entries
for each expert, collect the criteria weights judgments
for E1 to E4
- Collect the judgment of each criteria weight by using linguistic terms
- Transform to q-ROF numbers from linguistic terms
End
Aggregate the judgments of experts
for each expert, collect the criteria based alternative judgments
for E1 to E4
- Collect the judgment of each criteria based alternative by using linguistic terms
- Transform to q-ROF numbers from linguistic terms
End
Aggregate the judgments of experts
Calculate the criteria based alternative
Apply the steps of MAIRCA based on IVqROF number
Rank the alternative suppliers and find the best supplier
End

In the first stage of the application, 18 sub-criteria under 4 main criteria and 5 different alternatives (A1, A2…A5) were determined using the experience of 4 experts (E1, E2, E3, E4). The obtained data through a comprehensive literature research and the opinions of the experts are presented in Table 2. Expert 1 is the general coordinator who has over 20 years of experience in the business and has visited the suppliers determined as alternatives. Expert 2 is the purchasing manager who has been working in the business for 8 years. Expert 3 is the purchasing engineer who currently carries out purchasing activities in the business, Expert 4 is the stock manager who has been working in the industry for 15 years and extensive experience and deep technical knowledge about the product supplied.

The price criterion located under the economical criterion is the minimization type and is used to evaluate the high cost of the product to be supplied. The quality criterion is the maximization type and was utilized to handle the quality standards of supplier. Delivery time is the minimization type and was used to evaluate the length of delivery time offered by the supplier in line with its location and logistics management. The technology capacity is the maximization type and was employed to handle the pace of development and future production capabilities of supplier. The flexibility criterion is the maximization type and was utilized to handle the shortness of lead time, speed of resolving disputes, and adaptability of supplier.

Environment pollution control and environment management systems, which fall under the main environmental criterion, are maximization type criteria and were used to evaluate the abundance of the supplier's documentation on environmental management and the degree of procedures they have implemented to protect the environment from manufacturing waste. Eco-design recycling criterion is the maximization type and are used to evaluate the extent to which production waste is recycled. The green point is the maximization type and was used to evaluate how packaging waste is utilized by suppliers.

The occupational health and safety criterion, which is under the social main criterion, is the maximization type and is used to evaluate the occupational health and safety documents and procedures of the suppliers. The staff development criterion is the maximization type and was used to evaluate the supplier's personnel training. The local community effect is the maximization type and has been used to assess the supplier's returns to the community in which it resides. Information disclosure is the minimization type and is used to assess the supplier's rate of sharing and dissemination of existing data.

The criteria under the smart criterion are determined for smart supplier selection. Industry 4.0 staff and industry 4.0 utilization criteria are maximization type criteria and were used to evaluate the integration rate of the units and personnel within the supplier into smart technologies. The digital customer relations criterion is the maximization type and was used to evaluate the supplier's current infrastructure and speed that will enable the customer to quickly communicate their demands through the digital environment. The smart maintenance criterion is the maximization type and is used to evaluate the rate at which the supplier maintains the product it provides by using smart technologies such as artificial intelligence and the internet of things, detects its malfunction, repairs it or prevents it. The prediction ability criterion is the maximization type and was employed to handle the ability of supplier to forecast customer demand by analyzing historical customer data through smart technologies.

The weights of criteria were calculated using the interval-valued q-ROF number in line with the linguistic data collected from 4 experts. In the study, q = 3 was accepted. In the first stage, the opinions of experts were received from experts for 4 main criteria and 18 sub-criteria in line with linguistic data. Table 3 shows the linguistic terms and their IVq-ROF number scales. These scales are used to determine the importance degrees of criteria.

In the total gap matrix, the criterion ratings of each alternative were added as in Eq. (9), the weight degrees of the alternatives were calculated. The alternative with the smallest value among the obtained values was accepted as the best alternative. Table 17 shows the ranking of alternatives. In the ranking obtained by IVqROF numbers based MAIRCA, the most suitable smart supplier alternative for the business was found to be A2. A2 alternative is followed by A1-A4-A3 and A5 alternatives, respectively. A sensitivity analysis is performed on the impact of varying q values and the result is shown in Figure 1. Different q values present the same ranking for suppliers. Figure 2 presents a comparison analysis. The proposed method is compared with classic MAIRCA, VIKOR and TOPSIS methods. The results of the proposed method and classic MAIRCA are the same. The results of the proposed method, classic VIKOR and TOPSIS are the same except A3 and A5. This shows that the proposed method is useful for supplier selection problem.

FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTIONS

The limitation of this chapter is to define the weights of the criteria by using an aggregation operator. It aims to use a pairwise comparison matrix among criteria in future studies. This proposed new MCDM (IVqROF numbers based MAIRCA) method can be used in all complex decision making problems involving conflicting and uncertain criteria, except for supplier selection or smart supplier selection problems. There are many MCDM methods in the literature and new methods continue to be added. In future studies, research can be conducted using interval-valued q-ROF number integration of different decision-making methods. Interval valued q-ROF numbers can be developed with new extensions and used as a basis for both MAIRCA method and other MCDM methods in the literature.

CONCLUSION

The concept of supply chain is an indication that no business has complete control over the production and delivery of the products it provides to the customer. The participation of other businesses involved throughout all processes and the interactions between different parties are also important. In this period where increasingly strong competition prevails under the influence of changing environmental and social factors in recent years and businesses strive to provide competitive advantage, a strong supply chain is considered the key to companies' continued success. For this reason, in order to build strong supply chains, businesses examine the links that make up the supply chain and make efforts to improve, strengthen and make each of them sustainable. In this improvement process, they include their suppliers in the process with performance scoring reports and development programs.

Supply chain management has become very important in real life businesses and literature due to increasing globalization. Businesses aim to establish strategic collaborations with the most ideal suppliers in order to increase their competitiveness by building efficient supply chains. Choosing the right supplier will significantly reduce the total cost, as the supplier selection decisions are very effective in the profitability of the business and directly affect the delivery times of the enterprises. However, this process is complex and difficult because supplier selection may involve multiple conflicting and unclear criteria.

In its simplest form, a decision problem can be thought of as making a choice among options according to a goal or criterion. Decision makers need accurate and reliable predictions for the decisions they will make. Taking scientific criteria into consideration while doing this enables them to make better decisions. Classical MCDM techniques are often not sufficient to evaluate these unclear and contradictory criteria.

In this study, MAIRCA method based on interval valued q-ROF numbers, which is not included in the literature, is proposed to evaluate conflicting and uncertain criteria. This new proposal was applied on the smart supplier selection problem in an automotive supplier industry company. In addition to the traditional criteria, smart criteria have been added with the detailed literature study while determining the criteria for smart supplier selection. In the study, interval valued q-ROF numbers were used to reflect the uncertainties in the statements of the experts to the problem. In order to investigate the weights of the criteria constituting the concept of smart supplier selection for alternatives, the linguistic expression definitions of the experts were transformed into fuzzy numerical expressions by using IVqROF numbers based MAIRCA.
